paper_metadata.title: Long-term seizure outcome and risk factors for recurrence after extratemporal epilepsy surgery

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study describes a consecutive cohort from a specific comprehensive epilepsy program with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and detailed baseline characteristics. The recruitment period and setting are well-defined.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Patients who underwent extratemporal resection at the Comprehensive Epilepsy Program at Austin Health, Australia between 1991 and 2004.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as patients from a specific clinical program within a set timeframe.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: We included the entire cohort, with an examination of the effect of site of surgery and years of surgery.
items.reasoning: The study uses a whole-cohort approach from a specialized center, minimizing selection bias within that setting.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between 1991 and 2004.
items.reasoning: The dates are explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Comprehensive Epilepsy Program at Austin Health, Australia
items.reasoning: The specific clinical setting and location are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Included were patients who underwent extratemporal resection... Excluded were eight patients who had previous epilepsy surgery
items.reasoning: Clear inclusion and exclusion criteria are provided, including the rationale for exclusions.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: This resulted in a study cohort of n = 81.
items.reasoning: The study included the 'entire cohort' available at the center during the specified period.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Thirty-eight cases (47%) were male. Median age at surgery was 27.5 years... Median duration of preoperative epilepsy was 15.9 years.
items.reasoning: Key demographics and clinical history (age, sex, duration of epilepsy, pathology) are detailed.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study reports 0% loss to follow-up for the primary analysis, which is exceptional for a long-term study. Reasons for 'attrition' (death) are clearly documented and accounted for in the survival analysis.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: All cases had current follow-up (within 2 years); none were lost to follow-up.
items.reasoning: The authors explicitly state that no patients were lost to follow-up.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: we conducted a telephone interview if patients had not had medical follow-up for 2 years or more.
items.reasoning: The methodology for capturing data on those not seen in person is described.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: Eight cases had <5 years followup; all were deceased before the 5-year postoperative anniversary.
items.reasoning: The only 'losses' were due to death, and these were documented.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: At the time of death only one patient had remained seizure-free from surgery.
items.reasoning: The outcomes of those who died are described.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: none were lost to follow-up.
items.reasoning: Since there was no loss to follow-up other than death (which is an endpoint in itself), this bias is minimal.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors (pathology and resection extent) were assessed by single experts using standardized criteria (ILAE) and, crucially, were assessed blind to the outcome.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Histopathology findings were classified as: 1 Lesion... 2 Acquired insult... 3 Cortical dysplasia... 4 Nonspecific pathology
items.reasoning: The prognostic factors are clearly categorized and defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: All assessment was made blind to outcome.
items.reasoning: Blinding of the neuropathologist and neuroradiologist to the outcome is a strong safeguard against measurement bias.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Each variable was split into two groups for analysis by dividing cases at the median value.
items.reasoning: The use of medians for splitting continuous variables is a standard, non-data-dependent approach.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: One neuropathologist (RMK) reported all operative specimens... All available postoperative MRI scans were assessed by one neuroradiologist (LAM).
items.reasoning: Consistency is ensured by having single experts review all cases.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: In cases where one or both of the preoperative or postoperative scans were missing, all available radiologic evidence... were reviewed.
items.reasoning: Some data were missing or of poor quality (n=9 for resection extent), though the authors attempted to mitigate this with other records.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The study does not mention statistical imputation for missing prognostic factor data; it uses available case analysis or 'other' categories.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure recurrence) is clearly defined, but its measurement relies on a mix of medical records and telephone interviews (recall), which introduces potential for recall bias, especially for events occurring years prior.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Seizure recurrence was any postoperative disabling seizure (complex partial seizure [CPS] ± secondary generalization).
items.reasoning: The outcome is explicitly defined using standard clinical terminology.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Outcome data were collected from medical records and communications from treating doctors... interviewed by telephone if no follow-up data were available
items.reasoning: While standard for the field, telephone interviews and retrospective record reviews are subject to recall bias and vary in reliability compared to prospective diaries.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients who underwent surgery before 1997 were interviewed by telephone... Patients who underwent surgery from 1997 onward (n = 49) had routine follow-up
items.reasoning: There was a difference in how data were collected between the earlier and later parts of the cohort (retrospective vs. more systematic follow-up).

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses multivariable Cox regression to adjust for key potential confounders like pathology and extent of resection. It also specifically tests for the effect of 'year of surgery' to account for technological changes over time.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: Other variables to be examined included histopathology and completeness of resection... age at surgery and duration of preoperative epilepsy
items.reasoning: The study identifies and measures the most clinically relevant confounders for epilepsy surgery outcomes.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: Histopathology findings were classified as... Extent of resection was classified as...
items.reasoning: The categories for the main confounders are well-defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: All assessment was made blind to outcome.
items.reasoning: As with the PF, the confounders were measured by experts blinded to the outcome.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: One neuropathologist (RMK) reported all operative specimens... assessed by one neuroradiologist (LAM).
items.reasoning: Centralized review ensures consistency in confounder measurement.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: No imputation was performed for missing confounder data.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The study did not use matching or stratification in the design phase; it relied on statistical adjustment.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: A multivariate analysis was conducted using Cox proportional hazard regression.
items.reasoning: Multivariable modeling is the appropriate statistical method for adjusting for confounders in this study design.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods (Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier) are appropriate for time-to-event data. The authors provide hazard ratios and CIs, and the model building strategy is transparent.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models examined potential preoperative and perioperative risk factors
items.reasoning: The analytical plan is clearly laid out in the methods section.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: Entry into the multivariate regression was determined by preliminary univariate analysis of each variable; the threshold for inclusion... was p £ 0.10
items.reasoning: The study uses a standard p-value threshold for variable selection in the multivariable model.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: calculated using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis... multivariate analysis was conducted using Cox proportional hazard regression.
items.reasoning: Survival analysis is the gold standard for longitudinal prognosis studies.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Table 3. Preliminary analysis of potential risk factors... Table 4. Multivariate analysis
items.reasoning: The authors report both univariate and multivariate results for all pre-specified variables, including non-significant ones.
